acceptance: The alarm no longer fires when the calibrated metric is within threshold, or the reason for using raw time is documented
The issue body states which metric triggered the alarm
context: Found while reviewing open GitHub issues on 2026-11-12.
description:
## Problem
The trunk duration trend alarm (GitHub issue BenchBox-dev/benchbox#3511) sets status alarm from the raw "fast-junit summed test time" metric. On 2026-11-12 that rose 21.6% while the same metric divided by runner calibration fell 2.0%, and the earlier alarm showed raw +56.9% against calibration-normalised -14%. The alarm therefore reports runner-speed variation as a test-time regression, and the issue stays open without an actionable cause.

## Change
Decide which metric should trigger the alarm. If calibration is trustworthy, alarm on the calibrated metric and keep the raw one as context; otherwise state why the raw value is the signal. Note the 1-day window samples only 3 junit runs, so a minimum sample size may also be needed.
